content_preview.title: JetBrains Opens Early Access for Air Inside Its IDEs, Bringing Parallel Agent Sessions to the Editor Without Bundling an Agent
content_preview.summary: JetBrains has opened an early access program for Air in its IDEs, available as a Marketplace plugin or in 2026.3 EAP builds, and designed to run agents users already have.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JetBrains has launched an early access program for Air inside its IDEs. According to [the JetBrains Blog](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/10/air-in-ides-eap/), the program is available as a plugin on JetBrains Marketplace or natively in the 2026.3 EAP builds of JetBrains IDEs. [SD Times](https://sdtimes.com/ai/sd-times-news-roundup-oct-1-2026-ibm-bob-jetbrains-air-qodo-3-0/) carried the announcement in its October 1, 2026 news roundup, describing Air as an open system of products...

editor_notes.content_quality: 713 words (News range 400-1200). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Specifics (Ctrl double-tap, temporary worktrees, cloud runs for orgs with AI seats, per-session cost, privacy statements, Junie Lite) all trace to the JetBrains post.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (gunzip). manifest suspicious_patterns is null for all three; no injection text found. source-0 (blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/10/air-in-ides-eap/, 200): confirms EAP as Marketplace plugin or 2026.3 EAP builds; verbatim quote 'is a conduit for agents and subscriptions you already use. It is not an AI provider, and it ships with no agents installed.' appears exactly; Codex, GitHub Copilot, Junie, Cursor and other ACP-compatible agents; Claude subscription in terminal/full-screen tab; no JetBrains AI subscription needed; sessions view, Ctrl double-tap, tabs, worktrees, cloud 'Currently available to orgs with AI seats'; skills/tools list and 'for some tasks, use fewer tokens'; 'We believe... Junie Lite for free'; 'AI Assistant remains available'; 'Over time, we expect Air to become the primary experience'; 'an IDE that keeps agents at arm's length will struggle to stay relevant'; 'Air is a tool window, not an AI provider'; privacy and 'Air adds no new data processing terms'; 'Disable the Air plugin, and nothing else changes'. source-1 (sdtimes.com roundup, Archive.org fallback capture, 200 live): dated October 1, 2026 in the page; says Air is 'an open system of products for agentic development' launching EAP in 2026.3 EAP builds or Marketplace plugin; lists Codex, GitHub Copilot, Junie, Cursor, ACP agents; reproduces the IDE skills/tools paragraph verbatim. The article attributes only these to SD Times and attributes the Oct 1 date to SD Times, not to JetBrains in its own voice (the JetBrains post carries only a /2026/10/ URL and 'Last week/Today'). Details only JetBrains states (cloud, worktrees, privacy, Junie Lite) are attributed to JetBrains. source-2 (blog.jetbrains.com/air/2026/09/introducing-air-teams/): confirms 'team layer for agentic development', available to JetBrains business customers, expansion 'beyond a standalone desktop app' to individuals/teams/organizations, and 10 Automation templates including code review, bug fixes, dependency upgrades, documentation maintenance. Supports only what it is cited for. The 'September' label derives from the URL path; the snapshot text has no explicit date, which is a minor inference.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Title 'Without Bundling an Agent' is supported by 'ships with no agents installed' and 'tool window, not an AI provider'; Air is bring-your-own-agent via detection and ACP. Minor nuance: the FAQ says Air supports Codex, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Claude Agent and Junie 'out of the box' (integration, not bundling), and Junie Lite free runs require a JetBrains Account; the article's wording ('ships with no agents installed', quoted) stays accurate. Scope: 'JetBrains IDEs' generically; the sources name no specific IDEs or platforms, and the article does not claim any. 'AI Assistant remains available for now' is a fair paraphrase (FAQ: remains available and supported as a separate plugin). Early access, no GA date: correct. Cross-reference: /article/2026-03/25-jetbrains-unveils-central-... exists on disk and states Air entered public preview in March; also 2026-03/16 article covers Air preview. Link form is correct (singular article).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; promotional statements ('better results', 'fewer tokens', 'future of agentic development') are attributed to JetBrains and the article notes no independent testing exists.
editor_notes.originality: No prior article on the Air-in-IDEs EAP. Existing coverage is 2026-03/16 (Air preview) and 2026-03/25 (Central); no Air Teams or EAP article found in 2026-09/10. New development, not a duplicate.
concerns: The 'September' dating of the Air Teams post rests on the URL path only; minor.

The 'What We Don't Know' item on cloud pricing could also have noted the FAQ line that a JetBrains AI subscription is currently required for cloud runs; the article's 'orgs with AI seats' is consistent with it.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, correctly sourced. Link set matches the sources array exactly (3 external URLs plus one internal article link that resolves). Allowlist: blog.jetbrains.com and sdtimes.com both present. APPROVE.
